narratives.Overview:
## Summary

CodeQL open alert on default branch: **HIGH** `js/polynomial-redos` — Polynomial regular expression used on uncontrolled data.

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Alert | [#115](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/115) |
| Rule | `js/polynomial-redos` |
| Severity | HIGH |
| Location | `packages/core/src/doctor/manifest.ts` ~L154 |
| Message | This regular expression that depends on library input may run slow on strings with many repetitions of '/'. |

## What to build

Rewrite or bound the flagged site so CodeQL `js/polynomial-redos` clears for this alert (or document accepted risk with suppress + rationale if false positive after review). Prefer a real fix over suite-config changes.

## Acceptance

- [ ] CodeQL alert [#115](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/115) clears on master (auto-close or dismiss with reason after fix).
- [ ] Existing unit tests for the touched module still pass; add adversarial input coverage if useful.
- [ ] CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed entry citing CodeQL alert #115.

## Non-goals

- Changing CodeQL suite config as the primary fix.
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts into this issue (siblings tracked separately).

## In plain English
CodeQL alert #115 flags containDepositInstallRoot in doctor/manifest.ts L154 because trimmed.replace(/\\/g, "/").replace(/\/+$/, "") applies /\/+$/ to library input (raw install-root strings) and CodeQL reports slow matching on many "/" repetitions. Prefer-A rewrites that trailing-slash strip (and the normalize+strip chain on that line) to a linear helper so alert #115 clears by a real fix. Changing CodeQL suite config or suppress-as-primary stays a keep-out. Sibling AGENTS.md install-root regexes (INSTALLED_IN_RE / FULL_GUIDELINES_RE) are not this alert and stay out of file_scope unless tip evidence shows they are the same finding.

## Draft remedy sketch
1. Rewrite the L154 normalize+strip chain off /\/+$/ — prefer packages/core/src/text/redos-safe.ts stripTrailingPathSeparators (already linear; handles trailing / and \) plus a linear backslash-to-slash normalize for interior separators, or an equivalent non-backtracking helper colocated/imported so containDepositInstallRoot keeps the same posix path shape before the .. / absolute / containment checks.
2. Keep containDepositInstallRoot acceptance and rejection behavior for ordinary .deft/core, empty/null, absolute, .. segments, and escaping symlink cases covered by branches.test.ts.
3. Add adversarial coverage for long trailing-/ padded install-root strings that previously stressed the /\/+$/ shape; existing unit tests stay green.
4. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed entry citing CodeQL alert #115 / #5744.
5. Keep-out: CodeQL suite-config / path-exclude / suppress as the primary fix (issue Non-goals).

## Reject (draft)
- Treating CodeQL config / suppress / dismiss-without-fix as the primary remedy
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts into this issue
- Rewriting INSTALLED_IN_RE / FULL_GUIDELINES_RE / parseInstallRootFromAgentsMd as co-equal limbs of this Prefer-A without tip evidence they are alert #115
- Changing containment / ProjectionContainmentError / FALLBACK_INSTALL_ROOT semantics beyond what the L154 rewrite requires
- Claiming alert #115 cleared without a tip rewrite (or an evidence-backed false-positive disposition after review)

## file_scope lean (draft)
packages/core/src/doctor/manifest.ts; packages/core/src/text/redos-safe.ts only if a shared helper lands or is reused; packages/core/src/doctor/branches.test.ts (or adjacent adversarial fixtures); CHANGELOG.md.

Verdict: no blocking refutation of Prefer-A. The pinned L154 chain contains the reported backtracking shape; reusing the linear helper is a valid narrow remedy. One sharpening finding changes the adversarial test prescription.

### F1 — sharpens-framing — Exercise failed suffix matches, not only trailing slash padding

Evidence: draft comment 6256845942 step 3 specifies long trailing-slash padding. At the dispatch SHA, manifest.ts L154 applies the unanchored-start regex /\/+$/ after backslash normalization. A slash run at the end matches successfully; a slash run followed by a non-slash forces repeated unsuccessful suffix attempts. I extracted and executed the exact normalization statement from git show at the dispatch SHA in Node (no repository edits). For 'custom/' + '/'.repeat(n) + 'x', n=4,000/8,000/16,000 took approximately 4.9/22.8/78.4 ms; the corresponding trailing-only inputs took 0.080/0.014/0.023 ms. These are illustrative local measurements, not portable timing thresholds.

Failure mode: a regression test containing only trailing separators can pass with the vulnerable implementation intact. The raw library argument is untrusted; a relative prefix passes the early absolute-path guard, and downstream containment runs only after the expensive normalization. Later rejection cannot protect this CPU boundary.

Disposition consequence: Prefer-A can bind with the test wording sharpened to require a long interior slash run followed by a non-slash sentinel, plus the backslash equivalent (normalization creates the same slash run). Retain trailing-only cases for output parity. Exercise the exported containment path as well as any helper-level performance check; preserve exact output/fallback behavior, and use a generous bounded runtime check rather than the measured millisecond values above.

### F2 — footnote — Existing mechanisms support the narrow fix; no new containment layer is needed

Pin-read inventory: redos-safe.ts already exports stripTrailingPathSeparators, which scans backward over slash/backslash and slices once; redos-safe.test.ts covers trailing slash, trailing backslash, all-slash, and unchanged strings. manifest.ts already imports that module. The current /\\/g backslash substitution is a single-character global match, with no variable-length ambiguous quantifier; it can remain as the linear normalization step. Keeping trim and the existing absolute-path guard, then using stripTrailingPathSeparators(trimmed.replace(/\\/g, '/')), preserves the normalized string transformation without introducing another helper.

The pinned containment implementation already rejects empty results and '..' segments, checks resolved relative containment, and invokes assertProjectionContained. Pin-read projection-containment.ts confirms existing-component/realpath checks for escaping symlinks; branches.test.ts covers traversal, absolute/empty/null input, normal and uncreated custom roots, and escaping symlinks. Preserve these controls and supplement mixed-separator parity cases; do not claim they are absent or redesign them under this alert.

Road not taken: an explicit length bound could cap the cost, but introduces new rejection semantics and a threshold contract where an existing linear helper removes the problematic mechanism directly. Suppression would need evidence that the alert does not apply; the pinned statement and local failure-suffix reproduction support a real fix. Neither sibling parser regex is necessary to this remedy. Actual CodeQL clearance remains an implementation/delivery acceptance check, not something this critique has established.

Verification scope: issue body and the three named comments through the envelope ceiling; SHA-pinned source/tests/contract plus the isolated statement reproduction above. No later comments read, no product code changed, no full suite or CodeQL run. Round-1 critic complete; return to the parent for disposition. No further round seated.

**Lean:** Prefer-A — rewrite containDepositInstallRoot L154 trailing-slash strip off /\/+$/; reuse redos-safe stripTrailingPathSeparators; lock failed-suffix adversarial fixtures; keep suite-config suppress out.

## In plain English
CodeQL alert #115 is a real ReDoS shape on the L154 /\/+$/ strip after backslash normalize in containDepositInstallRoot. Prefer-A clears it by swapping that strip for the existing linear helper, not by silencing CodeQL. Codex Round-1 accepted the direction and sharpened one binding obligation: adversarial tests must exercise failed suffix matches (long slash run then a non-slash sentinel), because trailing-only padding can pass while the vulnerable regex remains.

## Bound remedy
1. **relieves: P1 — Rewrite L154 trailing-slash strip off /\/+$/.** Keep the linear single-character /\\/g backslash-to-slash normalize (Codex F2 inventory). Replace .replace(/\/+$/, "") with stripTrailingPathSeparators from packages/core/src/text/redos-safe.ts (already imported via that module path in manifest.ts), or an equivalent non-backtracking strip. Preserve containDepositInstallRoot outcomes for ordinary .deft/core, empty/null, absolute, .. segments, uncreated custom roots, and escaping symlink fallbacks covered by branches.test.ts.
2. **relieves: P1 — Lock failed-suffix adversarial fixtures (Codex F1).** Require fixtures with a long interior slash run followed by a non-slash sentinel (and the backslash equivalent that normalizes into the same slash run). Retain trailing-only cases for output parity only — they are not sufficient ReDoS regression alone. Exercise the exported containDepositInstallRoot path; if a helper-level timing check is used, keep it generous/bounded and do not hard-code the local millisecond measurements from Round-1. Supplement mixed-separator parity cases without redesigning containment.
3. **relieves: P1 — Tip CodeQL / delivery evidence for alert #115.** Report functional compatibility and master alert #115 closure as separate evidence rows. Actual CodeQL clearance is an implementation acceptance check (Codex F2).
4. **relieves: P1 — CHANGELOG Security/Fixed for alert #115 / #5744.**

### Reject
- CodeQL suite-config / path-exclude / suppress / dismiss-without-fix as the primary remedy
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts
- Co-equal rewrite of INSTALLED_IN_RE / FULL_GUIDELINES_RE / parseInstallRootFromAgentsMd without tip evidence they are alert #115
- Explicit length-bound / new rejection threshold as the primary P1 control (Codex road-not-taken)
- Claiming a new containment layer is required (Codex F2: existing assertProjectionContained / .. / absolute guards suffice)
- Claiming P1 relieved from trailing-only padding examples or a green unit suite alone
- Changing FALLBACK_INSTALL_ROOT / ProjectionContainmentError semantics beyond what the L154 rewrite requires

### Disposition of Round-1
- Codex F1 (sharpens-framing) -> accept-into-contract as limb 2
- Codex F2 (footnote) -> accept inventory; keep /\\/g; reuse stripTrailingPathSeparators; no new containment layer
- Prefer-A direction survives; empty disagreement set on blocks-the-design

Verdict: Prefer-A Bound 6256889738 honestly covers Stop 1 P1 as a remedy contract. No blocking, sharpening, or footnote findings; no Recut required. This is design relief, not a claim that the fix has shipped or alert #115 has closed.

I independently pin-read manifest.ts and redos-safe.ts at the dispatch SHA. containDepositInstallRoot still performs the flagged trailing-slash regex after trim, the absolute-path guard, and backslash normalization, but before its containment checks. A relative prefix plus a slash run plus a non-slash sentinel reaches that operation; downstream containment cannot prevent its failed-suffix matching cost.

Limb 1 removes that precise mechanism. The existing stripTrailingPathSeparators scans backward with a strictly decreasing index and slices once. After the retained backslash-to-slash normalization, its additional ability to strip backslashes cannot change the result: no backslashes remain. Thus the substitution preserves the normalized value supplied to the existing empty-result, traversal, relative-containment, and projection-containment guards. No new threshold or containment layer is needed.

Limb 2 incorporates the substantive Round-1 objection: failed-suffix slash and normalized-backslash fixtures through the exported function, with trailing-only inputs explicitly limited to parity evidence. It does not substitute successful trailing matches for adversarial coverage or bind tests to the prior machine's timings.

Limb 3 keeps functional compatibility separate from actual master CodeQL closure. That prevents a green unit suite or this audit from being reported as alert clearance. Limb 4 supplies the issue's changelog obligation; it is supporting delivery evidence, not independently the CPU-risk control. Read together, the four limbs cover P1 without claiming any existing implementation result.

The strongest alternative is a length cap, which could bound exposure, but would add rejection semantics where the existing linear helper removes the cause. Suppression would require contrary evidence about applicability; the pinned reachable operation supports the direct rewrite. Neither alternative exposes an unmet obligation in this Bound remedy.

Verification scope: issue body, the three named comments within the ceiling, SHA-pinned source, and Contract Critic method/pain-audit obligations.
